name: Shape-memory alloy distractor

lead: A shape-memory alloy distractor is an implantable device made of nickel-titanium (nitinol) that gradually pushes two cut bone segments apart. Because the metal returns to a pre-set shape as it warms to body temperature, it can do this without a patient or surgeon turning a screw. The aim in appearance-related surgery is to grow new bone, for example to build up jaw bone or lengthen the mandible, with a fully buried device.

Published studies are laboratory and animal studies, mainly on dog jaws in China and one later US-journal paper. They report that new bone filled the gap and eventually matched surrounding bone in density and strength. Wikipedia describes shape-memory distractors as under research as of 2013 rather than an established clinical option.

paras: In the animal studies, surgeons cut a box-shaped or complete osteotomy in the jaw, placed the buried alloy distractor, and let it expand by itself while the bone healed over weeks to months. In looksmaxxing discussion it appears as a research curiosity for height and jaw lengthening ideas; it is not something people can currently obtain as a routine procedure.

Distraction osteogenesis in general involves surgery, infection risk, relapse and a long consolidation period. Nitinol contains nickel, which matters for people with nickel sensitivity. The shape-memory devices described in the literature are experimental, with outcomes known mainly from animal models.

Metal returns to its set shape and slowly separates the segments
New bone forms in the gap, lengthening or raising the bone
angle.text: The idea is to lengthen or raise bone, such as the jaw or alveolar ridge, using a fully buried device that moves itself. People interested in jaw or skeletal changes follow it as a research direction; published work so far is in animals.

lead: A shape-memory alloy (SMA) distractor is a bone-lengthening device made from a nickel-titanium alloy such as nitinol. It is used in distraction osteogenesis, the technique in which a surgeon cuts a bone and then slowly separates the pieces so new bone forms in the gap [1]. Conventional distractors are turned by hand or driven by a motor; an SMA distractor is built to move itself as the metal returns to a remembered shape [2].

The appeal for appearance-related surgery is a buried, self-activating device that could lengthen or raise bone, such as jaw bone, without an external hardware or daily adjustments. For this reason it is sometimes raised in discussions of jaw lengthening and height-related surgery.

Published research consists of animal studies, mostly in dog mandibles. They report that distraction gaps filled with new bone, that bone density and strength approached that of untreated bone after about six months, and that the devices could complete bone transport [3][4][5][6]. Wikipedia notes that SMA distractors were under research as of 2013 and not an established clinical option [1].

paras: Distraction osteogenesis proceeds in phases: the bone is cut and a device attached, a latency period of about a week follows, the segments are gradually separated (typically around 1 mm per day), and the device then holds them steady while the new bone consolidates [1]. A shape-memory distractor replaces the manual or motorised activation step with a metal element that exerts a steady force on its own.

Shape-memory alloys can be deformed when cold and recover a pre-set shape on warming, because they shift between martensite and austenite crystal phases [2]. Nitinol, a nickel-titanium alloy developed at the US Naval Ordnance Laboratory in the early 1960s, is the most common example and is already used in medical items such as bone staples, stents and orthodontic archwires [2]. In one dog study, the S-shaped distractors used 1 mm wire with a rebound temperature of 33 degrees C [4].

In a ten-dog study of mandibular alveolar ridge augmentation, bone segments rose 7.5 to 11.5 mm within a week of implanting the distractors, regenerated bone was visible on radiographs at one month, and new and native bone could not be told apart clearly at three months, with no bone resorption seen [3].

A twelve-dog study found that bone density and compressive strength in the augmented ridge were lower than control at three months but showed no significant difference by six months, leading the authors to conclude the new bone was strong enough for implant placement [5]. A related study combining the distractor with acellular dermal matrix reported higher bone density and strength on the treated side than on the control side [4].

A study of 18 dogs compared osteotomy techniques with a buried, self-activated distractor, finding that complete osteotomy produced a larger initial distraction space but a notable depression at the distracted area, while partial osteotomy preserved the lingual cortex [6]. Another group designed an internal elastic distraction device for trifocal bone transport in a canine mandibular defect; regenerated bone formed in two months, though the chin region was not fully reconstructed because of the narrow angle and thick soft tissue there [7].

No studies found in human patients. The published work identified consists of canine mandible experiments [3][4][5][6][7]. General reviews of jaw distraction osteogenesis note significant vertical relapse and evidence too limited for meta-analysis [1].

General risks of distraction osteogenesis include surgery, device removal in a second operation for conventional systems, and relapse [1]. Nitinol is roughly 55 to 60 percent nickel by weight [2]. The animal studies above did not report on human tolerability.
